items.title: Four More Afflictions That Surface in Solitary Practice, and Their Remedies

items.zh: 一、於奢摩他、毘鉢舍那品有闇昧心。二、於諸定有隨愛味。三、於生有隨動相心。四、推後後日，顧待餘時，隨不死尋，不能熾然勤修方便。
items.en: First, a mind clouded with confusion regarding calm-abiding and insight. Second, craving that clings to states of concentration. Third, a mind still stirred by attraction towards future rebirth. Fourth, pushing practice off to some later day, waiting for another time, following the thought "I will not die yet" — and so failing to apply oneself with real intensity.

items.zh: 如是四種所對治法，當知亦有四種修習對治。一、修光明想；二、修離欲想；三、修滅想；四、修死想。
items.en: For these four afflictions, four cultivations likewise serve as remedy: cultivating the perception of light; cultivating the perception of freedom from craving; cultivating the perception of cessation; and cultivating the perception of death.

items.title: Impurity-Contemplation Unpacked: Twelve Obstacles at Two Stages of Practice

items.zh: 又不淨想略有二種。一、思擇力攝，二、修習力攝。
items.en: Impurity-contemplation, in brief, is of two kinds: that grounded in the power of reflection, and that grounded in the power of cultivation.

items.zh: 思擇力攝不淨想中，當知五法為所對治。何等為五？一、親近母邑。二、處顯失念。三、居隱放逸。四、通處隱顯由串習力。五、雖勤方便修習不淨，而作意錯亂。謂不觀不淨，隨淨相轉，如是名為作意錯亂。修習力攝不淨想中，當知七法為所對治。何等為七？謂本所作事心散亂性。本所作事趣作用性。方便作意不善巧性，由不恭敬勤請問故。又由不能守根門故；雖處空閑，猶有種種染污尋思擾亂其心。又於飲食不知量故，身不調適。又為尋思所擾亂故，不樂遠離內心寂靜奢摩他定。又由彼身不調適故，不能善修毘鉢舍那，不能如實觀察諸法。如是一切所對治法，當知總說一門十二，一門十四。又即如是所對治法，能治白法還有爾所。於修二種不淨想中，當知多有所作。
items.en: In the impurity-contemplation grounded in the power of reflection, it should be understood that five things are to be remedied. What are the five? First, keeping close company with women. Second, losing mindfulness in public places. Third, being heedless in private places. Fourth, in both private and public places, being carried along by the force of habit. Fifth, although diligently applying oneself to cultivating impurity, one's attention is confused: that is, not contemplating impurity, one follows the sign of attractiveness; this is called confused attention. In the impurity-contemplation grounded in the power of cultivation, it should be understood that seven things are to be remedied. What are the seven? The distraction of the mind by one's former activities; the mind's inclination towards the business of those former activities; lack of skill in applying attention to the practice, because one does not respectfully and diligently ask questions. Further, because one cannot guard the doors of the senses, even while in a secluded place all kinds of defiled thoughts still disturb one's mind. Further, because one does not know moderation in eating, the body is not well-adjusted. Further, because one is disturbed by thoughts, one does not delight in the calm-abiding concentration of seclusion and inner quiet. Further, because the body is not well-adjusted, one cannot cultivate insight well and cannot examine phenomena as they truly are. All these things to be remedied, it should be understood, number twelve by one way of counting and fourteen by another. Further, there are as many bright qualities that remedy these things to be remedied. In cultivating the two kinds of impurity-contemplation, it should be understood that there is much to be done.

items.title: Contemplating Suffering Within Impermanence: Six Obstacles to Overcoming Laziness

items.zh: 又於無常所修苦想，略有六種所對治法。
items.en: For contemplating suffering within impermanence, there are, in brief, six obstacles to be remedied.

items.zh: 何等為六？一、於未生善法最初應生，而有嬾墮。二、於已生善法應住不忘、修習圓滿、倍令增廣所有懈怠；三、於恭敬師長往請問中，不恒相續。四、於恒修善法常隨師轉，遠離淨信。五、由遠離淨信，不能常修。六、於內放逸，由放逸故，於常修習諸善法中，不恒隨轉。如是六種所對治法，還有六法能為對治，多有所作。與此相違，應知其相。又光明想，緣多光明以為境界，如三摩呬多地中已說。今此義中，意辯緣法光明以為境界，修光明想。
items.en: What are the six? First, laziness with regard to giving rise for the first time to wholesome qualities not yet arisen. Second, slackness with regard to wholesome qualities already arisen, which ought to be maintained without being forgotten, cultivated to completion, and made to increase and expand. Third, not going continuously and respectfully to one's teachers and elders to ask questions. Fourth, being far from pure faith in the constant cultivation of wholesome qualities and in always following one's teacher. Fifth, because one is far from pure faith, being unable to cultivate constantly. Sixth, inner heedlessness; because of heedlessness, not keeping continuously to the constant cultivation of wholesome qualities. For these six things to be remedied there are, in turn, six things that act as their remedies, and there is much to be done. Their characteristics should be understood as the opposite of these. Further, light-perception takes abundant light as its object, as already explained in the Ground of Concentration. In the present meaning, the intention is to explain the cultivation of light-perception that takes the light of the teaching as its object.

items.title: Light-Perception: What "Light" Actually Means in This Practice

items.zh: 謂如所聞已得究竟不忘念法，名法光明，與彼俱行彼相應想，應知名光明想。
items.en: The teaching one has heard, thoroughly retained and never forgotten, is called the light of the teaching. The perception that arises together with and corresponds to that light should be known as light-perception.

items.zh: 何以故？真實能令心闇昧者，謂方便修止觀品時，於諸法中所有忘念。與此相違，當知即是光明。
items.en: Why is this so? What truly makes the mind dark is forgetfulness regarding the teachings while one is practising the aspects of calm-abiding and insight. The opposite of this should be understood as light.

blocks.text: The obstacles of solitary practice, and detailed lists of what obstructs impurity contemplation and diligence. Several of the lists are missing from Ru-Yi's translation; the English column gives our own translation, and the commentary summarises them.

subs.head: Four obstacles in solitude, four perceptions

blocks.text: In solitary practice four afflictions arise: confusion regarding calm and insight; craving for concentration; fear of nirvāṇa; and the wish to put things off, "waiting for another time". The remedies are four perceptions: of **light**, of **freedom from craving**, of **cessation**, and of **death**. Venerable Miào Jìng on the last: "if one breath fails to come, you die; what other time is there?" The craving meant is not sense craving but craving for meditative states.

(Missing from Ru-Yi's translation; the English column gives our own.) Impurity contemplation is of two kinds. At the stage of **reflection**, five things obstruct it: keeping company with the opposite sex; losing mindfulness in public; heedlessness in private; habit in both; and misdirected attention that follows the attractive rather than the impure. Master Cháng Bǎi: desire is like wearing a straw cloak near a fire. At the stage of **cultivation**, seven obstruct it: distraction by former tasks; inclination to busy activity; unskilful method from not asking for instruction; unguarded senses; immoderate eating; dislike of calm; and inability to practise insight.

(Missing from Ru-Yi's translation; the English column gives our own.) Laziness towards good not yet arisen; indolence towards good already arisen; not consulting teachers continually; lacking pure faith in the teacher; therefore not practising constantly; and inner heedlessness. Master Cháng Bǎi: attention should be on the Dharma, not on persons; attachment to a person is only faith, not pure faith.

The perception of light here is not of sun, moon, or lamp. "The teaching one has heard, thoroughly retained and never forgotten, is called the light of the teaching." The perception that arises with it, recollecting the teaching with understanding, is light-perception. Venerable Miào Jìng: it is not mere memory, but memory joined with wise observation.

quiz.q: What four afflictions does the treatise name in solitary practice?
options: confusion about calm and insight, craving for concentration, stirring towards birth, postponing practice thinking "I won't die yet"
quiz.why: "First, a mind clouded with confusion regarding calm-abiding and insight. Second, craving that clings to states of concentration. Third, a mind stirred regarding birth. Fourth, pushing practice off to some later day, following the thought 'I will not die yet.'"

quiz.q: What four perceptions remedy these, in order?
options: light, freedom from craving, cessation, death
quiz.why: "Cultivating the perception of light; of freedom from craving; of cessation; and of death." Venerable Miào Jìng: waiting for another time — if one breath doesn't come, you're dead; what other time is there?

quiz.q: In "perception of freedom from craving," what does Venerable Miào Jìng say the craving is?
options: desire-realm wealth, sex, fame, food, sleep
not desire-realm craving but craving within form and formless absorptions
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: this craving is not desire-realm craving but craving within the absorptions of the form and formless realms. It counters the second affliction, craving for concentration. Master Cháng Bǎi: meditative craving is stronger than the desires of a scattered mind.

quiz.q: On "pushing practice off to a later day, waiting for another time," how does Venerable Miào Jìng warn?
options: if one breath doesn't come you're dead — what other time is there?
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: you "wait for another time" — but if one breath fails to come you die; what other time is there? Hence the perception of death as remedy.

quiz.q: At what stage is impurity-contemplation "grounded in reflection," per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: at the stage of hearing and reflection
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the power of reflection belongs to the time of hearing and reflecting — impurity-contemplation at that stage. The power of cultivation belongs to calm-and-insight practice.

quiz.q: What image does Master Cháng Bǎi use for one with desire encountering the opposite sex?
options: like wearing a straw cloak — touching fire, it surely ignites
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with desire, one is like someone wearing a straw cloak; when a man or woman appears, the straw cloak touching fire is sure to catch.

quiz.q: What "light" does Master Cháng Bǎi say light-perception refers to here?
options: the light of the Dharma, not sun, moon, or lamp
light seen by the divine eye
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this is not the light of the sun, the moon, or a lamp, but cultivating the light of the Dharma. Venerable Miào Jìng: elsewhere the treatise speaks of lights of colours and elements; here it differs.
